title: Owandy Radiology Introduces AI Segmentation for QuickVision 3D
html:
By News Staff

November 23, 2026

Share

Owandy Radiology will introduce an artificial intelligence-powered segmentation feature for its QuickVision 3D implant planning software at the Greater New York Dental Meeting, November 29 through December 1, 2026, at the Jacob K. Javits Convention Center in New York.

The new feature automatically separates anatomical structures on cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) scans, allowing clinicians to examine individual structures during implant treatment planning. According to the company, the software identifies and separates the maxilla, mandible, individual teeth from crown to root, and anatomical canals, including the mandibular canal.

The segmentation capability is designed to help clinicians evaluate available bone volume, examine root anatomy, and identify anatomical structures that must be considered when planning implant placement. Clinicians are responsible for reviewing and validating the AI-generated segmentation before using the information for treatment planning.

When you re planning an implant, you need to see how the proposed site relates to the available bone, nearby roots and the mandibular canal, said Boris Loyez, vice president of sales and marketing for Owandy Radiology North America. By separating those structures automatically, QuickVision 3D gives clinicians a head start on reviewing the scan. They can verify the anatomy and use that information to plan implant placement more accurately and design the surgical guide in the same workflow.

QuickVision 3D enables clinicians to review panoramic and cross-sectional images, overlay digital impressions on CBCT data, and simulate implant placement using a library of implant models. The software also supports surgical guide design and export for 3D printing, allowing clinicians to incorporate the new segmentation capability into an existing digital planning workflow.

In addition to implant planning, the AI segmentation feature has potential applications in endodontics. By isolating individual teeth from crown to root on CBCT scans, the software allows clinicians to examine root anatomy and evaluate root canals, including those that may not be visible on conventional two-dimensional radiographs.

Owandy Radiology will demonstrate the new capability at booth 3614 during the Greater New York Dental Meeting.

Headquartered in France, with North American operations based in Garden City, New York, Owandy Radiology develops dental imaging hardware and software distributed through dental dealers in the United States and internationally.

More information is available at www.owandy.com.
